title: Memo: Does majority-vote ensembling improve accuracy?

yaml.title: Memo: Does majority-vote ensembling improve accuracy?
yaml.subtitle: Research memorandum — ensemble voting simulation
author: Jack J. Burleson
Grant Mooslin

markdown.markdown:
**Research question:** If we ran the classifier *K* times per image and took a majority vote, how much accuracy would we recover — and at what cost multiplier?

**Formal write-up:** [`montecarlo/ensemble-voting.qmd`](../montecarlo/ensemble-voting.html) · [`reports/monte_carlo/ensemble_accuracy_vs_k.md`](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone/blob/main/reports/monte_carlo/ensemble_accuracy_vs_k.md)

---


**Majority voting buys +4.2 *pp* at 25× cost, with diminishing returns after *K* = 7.** Simulated over the 1,512-image corpus (2,000 committee votes per image per *K*):

| *K* | Accuracy | 95% *CI* | Cost |
|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | 0.821 | 0.805–0.836 | 1× |
| 3 | 0.836 | 0.820–0.851 | 3× |
| 5 | 0.844 | 0.828–0.859 | 5× |
| 7 | 0.850 | 0.834–0.865 | 7× |
| 10 | 0.853 | 0.837–0.869 | 10× |
| 15 | 0.859 | 0.842–0.874 | 15× |
| 25 | 0.863 | 0.846–0.879 | 25× |

::: {.callout-warning title="Diminishing Returns"}
The curve is concave and flattening: ***K* = 3** gives 1.5 *pp* for 3×, ***K* = 7** gives 2.9 *pp* for 7×, and doubling to ***K* = 25** adds only 1.3 *pp* more. ***K* = 5–7 is the practical sweet spot** (2.3–2.9 *pp* at 5–7× cost).
:::

**Per-class:** the classes that gain most from voting are the hardest ones — `handwritten` 0.841 → 0.908 at *K* = 25 (+6.7 *pp*), `questionnaire` +6.2 *pp*, `resume` +4.9 *pp*, `budget` +5.1 *pp* — while `letter` is nearly flat (0.742 → 0.757, +1.5 *pp*) because its errors are systematic (`letter`↔`memo`), not random.

**Conclusion.** Ensembling recovers real accuracy but at a steep price and with diminishing returns; it helps most where errors are non-systematic and least where the model is deterministically wrong (the near-synonym pairs).

::: {.memo-sources}
*Sources:* `reports/monte_carlo/ensemble_accuracy_vs_k.md` · [github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone)
:::

---

## What questions or uncertainties remain?

The simulation reuses the *same model's* per-image prediction distribution (draws from observed correct/incorrect labels), so it measures label-noise averaging, not the benefit of *diverse* models. A heterogeneous committee (different models per vote) would likely beat same-model voting; that is untested.

## What other levers may also improve accuracy?

[Confidence-gated escalation](confidence-routing.qmd) targets the same error budget for 1.02–1.8× cost instead of 3–25× — strictly better on cost per *pp*. [Few-shot exemplars](exemplar-mining.qmd) attack the deterministic-error classes that voting cannot fix.
